items.item_text: Bachelors Degree.
Masters Degree.
Five (5) years of relevant full-time experience in higher education, student affairs, professional or health education setting.
Seven (7) years of relevant full-time experience in a higher education, student affairs, professional or medical education setting.
Four (4) years of experience in event planning, program coordination, operations coordination, project management or a closely related function.
Six (6) years of experience in event planning, executive communications, program coordinator, or project management.

Demonstrated experience independently managing projects, programs, or events from planning through implementation and follow-up, including development of timelines, coordination of activities, tracking progress, and evaluation of outcomes.
Three (3) years of experience supporting complex scheduling, travel coordination, and expense processing for a leader or program.
Experience managing relationships with vendors and external partners, including coordinating services, monitoring performance, and addressing issues to ensure successful program and event execution.
Independently manages logistical planning for Student Affairs events, including venue and space requests, vendor management, purchasing support, registration, and day-of execution support.
Develops and maintains event timelines, task lists, and run-of-show documents; monitors milestones; identifies risks or barriers; adjusts plans as needed.
Manages post-event wrap-up expense reconciliation, documentation and follow-up.
Solicits and summarizes post event feedback, identifies recurring operational themes and lessons learned and recommends improvement for future events.

Designs event documents for tracking event planning and deliverables and works with marketing and communications on event announcement elements (i.e., save the date, invitation, and calendar invitations).

Develops and distributes student-facing communications, including calendar postings, event reminders, OSA social media content, and digital or print communications; maintains media assets and utilizes established templates, processes, and communication channels to support student engagement initiatives.

Serves as operational owner of the student professional development funding program and manages the end-to-end administrative workflow for student professional development funding requests (intake, tracking, documentation, status updates, and recordkeeping).
Reviews requests for completeness and eligibility, coordinate required approvals , and maintain accurate logs of awards, reimbursements, and deadlines.
Develop and maintain student-facing guidance, timelines and process communications.
Manages assigned projects and initiatives sponsored by Student Affairs leadership including planning, coordination, implementation and follow-through.
Supports the project management, strategy, and communication development for annual reporting, program evaluation, policy & process development, strategic planning, and team development.
Drafts, proofreads, and formats correspondence, agendas, and routine communications.

Supports the development of standard and nonstandard communication materials such as presentations, handouts, spreadsheets, newsletters, status updates, and summaries using Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Canva.
Lead or support Student Affairs projects and operational initiatives as assigned.
Ability to manage multiple projects concurrently.
Ability and willingness to work flexible hours to support activities of the office, including some evenings and weekends.
Ability to identify operational issues, evaluate alternatives, and implement process improvements that support efficient and effective program operations.
